entries.en: k as in 'skin' (no puff of air)
entries.notes: Name: ko (ক). First letter of কেমন and কী.

entries.en: kh: k with a puff of air, as in 'kite'
entries.notes: Name: kho (খ). The aspirated partner of ক.

entries.en: g as in 'go'
entries.notes: Name: go (গ).

entries.en: gh: g with a breathy puff
entries.notes: Name: gho (ঘ). The aspirated partner of গ.

entries.en: ng as in 'sing' (never starts a word)
entries.notes: Name: ungo (উঙ). Same sound as the sign ং (s02-l07); only the spelling differs. Main use is inside conjuncts like ঙ্গ (লুঙ্গি).

entries.en: tree
cow
room / house
entries.notes: Also 'home' in a general sense; বাড়ি (bari) is the usual word for a house/home.

entries.en: Bengali (person)
entries.notes: Example of ঙ inside a word. Bangla Academy standard: colour is spelled রং on its own, রঙ only before an ending (রঙিন).

entries.en: ch as in 'church' (no puff)
entries.notes: Name: cho (চ).

entries.en: chh: ch with a strong puff of air
entries.notes: Name: chho (ছ). Aspirated partner of চ. First letter of ছাত্র.

entries.en: j as in 'jam'
entries.notes: Name: borgio jo (বর্গীয় জ). Same sound as য (ontostho jo); only spelling differs.

entries.en: jh: j with a breathy puff
entries.notes: Name: jho (ঝ). Aspirated partner of জ.

entries.en: n, found almost only inside conjuncts (ঞ্চ = 'nch')
entries.notes: Name: iyo (ইঁয়ো). Sounds like ন inside words (পঞ্চাশ ponchash). Never starts a common word.

entries.en: eye
storm
entries.notes: Ends with ড় (flapped r), taught in s02-l07.

entries.en: hard t, tongue curled back (like English 't' in 'top')
entries.notes: Name: to (ট). Retroflex. English t is closer to ট than to ত.

entries.en: hard t with a puff of air (not English 'th')
entries.notes: Name: tho (ঠ). Aspirated partner of ট.

entries.en: hard d, tongue curled back (like English 'd' in 'dog')
entries.notes: Name: do (ড). Look-alike: উ (vowel) has no headline notch; ড has a notch on top. ড় (with a dot) is a different sound (s02-l07).

entries.en: hard d with a breathy puff
entries.notes: Name: dho (ঢ). First letter of ঢাকা.

entries.en: n (same sound as ন; 'retroflex n' letter)
entries.notes: Name: murdhonno no (মূর্ধন্য ণ). Sounds like ন today; the difference is spelling only. Rarely starts a word.

entries.en: drum (traditional)
entries.notes: Two-headed folk drum played at weddings and Pohela Boishakh.

entries.en: soft t, tongue on the teeth (as in Spanish 'tú')
entries.notes: Name: to (ত). Dental. Its final no-vowel form is ৎ (s02-l07).

entries.en: soft t with a puff of air (not English 'th')
entries.notes: Name: tho (থ). Aspirated partner of ত. Look-alike: থ has a loop at the bottom; compare with ধ and য.

entries.en: soft d, tongue on the teeth
entries.notes: Name: do (দ). Dental.

entries.en: soft d with a breathy puff
entries.notes: Name: dho (ধ). First letter of ধন্যবাদ. Look-alike: ধ vs ব: ধ has a gap in the headline at top-left.

entries.en: n as in 'no'
entries.notes: Name: donto no (দন্ত্য ন). The everyday n letter; same sound as ণ.

entries.en: p as in 'spin' (no puff)
entries.notes: Name: po (প).

entries.en: f, or a puffed p (between 'ph' and 'f')
entries.notes: Name: fo/pho (ফ). Most Bangladeshis say a clear f (ফল fol).

entries.en: b as in 'bat'
entries.notes: Name: bo (ব), also borgio bo (বর্গীয় ব). Shape: a plain triangle hanging from the line. র is ব with a dot below.

entries.en: bh: breathy b, often close to 'v'
entries.notes: Name: bho (ভ). First letter of ভালো.

entries.en: m as in 'mother'
entries.notes: Name: mo (ম).

entries.en: j as in 'jam' (same sound as জ)
entries.notes: Name: ontostho jo (অন্তঃস্থ য). With a dot below it becomes য় (y), taught next lesson.

entries.en: r: a light tap of the tongue (like Spanish 'pero')
entries.notes: Name: bo-ye shunno ro (ব-য়ে শূন্য র), 'ব with a dot'. Never trill or curl it like English r.

entries.en: l as in 'love'
entries.notes: Name: lo (ল).

entries.en: sh as in 'shop'
entries.notes: Name: talobbo sho (তালব্য শ). The most common sh letter (শিক্ষক).

entries.en: sh as in 'shop' (same sound as শ)
entries.notes: Name: murdhonno sho (মূর্ধন্য ষ). Same sound as শ; spelling only. Rarely starts a word; common in the middle (মানুষ).

entries.en: sh, or s before t / n / r / l
entries.notes: Name: donto sho (দন্ত্য স). Usually 'sh' (সকাল shokal), but 's' in clusters like স্ত, স্ক (s04).

entries.en: h as in 'hat'
entries.notes: Name: ho (হ). Changes shape with some vowel signs: হু, হৃ (s03-l02).

entries.en: red
hand
flapped r: tongue curled back, flicked forward (like the tt in American 'butter')
entries.notes: Name: doye shunno ro (ড-য়ে শূন্য র), 'ড with a dot'. Encoded as ড + nukta (U+09A1 U+09BC). Sounds close to র; in casual BD speech often merges with it.

entries.en: flapped r with a puff of breath
entries.notes: Name: dhoye shunno ro (ঢ-য়ে শূন্য র). Encoded ঢ + nukta (U+09A2 U+09BC). Rare; usually said like ড়.

entries.en: y as in 'yes' (often a glide between vowels)
entries.notes: Name: ontostho o (অন্তঃস্থ অ). Encoded য + nukta (U+09AF U+09BC). Very common: মেয়ে, কোথায়.

entries.en: final t with no vowel after it
entries.notes: Name: khondo to (খণ্ড ত), 'broken t'. U+09CE. Only appears at the end of a syllable (হঠাৎ, উৎসব).

entries.en: ng as in 'sing' (nasal at the end of a syllable)
entries.notes: Name: onushshar (অনুস্বার). U+0982. Same sound as ঙ. Shown standalone here; fonts may draw a dotted circle.

entries.en: a short breath; inside a word it doubles the next consonant
entries.notes: Name: bishorgo (বিসর্গ). U+0983. দুঃখিত is said dukkhito: the ঃ makes the খ double. Shown standalone; fonts may draw a dotted circle.

entries.en: ঁ makes the vowel nasal (shown on আ: a~)
entries.notes: Sign: chondrobindu (চন্দ্রবিন্দু) ঁ, U+0981, 'moon and dot', written above the letter. Shown on আ because it cannot stand alone.

entries.en: dark / deep (of colour)
entries.notes: Uses ঢ়. গাঢ় লাল = deep red. Native check: pronunciation often closer to 'garo'.

entries.en: suddenly
sorry
entries.notes: 'I'm sorry' = আমি দুঃখিত (formal). Shows ঃ doubling the খ.

entries.en: moon
entries.notes: The transliteration guide's own example of ঁ.
